items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-20
items.q: It was Stranicos' man that we used to play over there with Charlie Wagner, Johnny Roniger, Meyer Weinberg, Doc Benitez.

ctx.x: Did Stranicos ever go over to the Gulf Coast? He was from the Gulf Coast.

Ellis was from the Gulf Coast. Yeah. It was Stranicos' man that we used to play over there with Charlie Wagner, Johnny Roniger, Meyer Weinberg, Doc Benitez. You know, he died recently. Oh, yes, he did, yeah. Doc died. Three bass players that worked with me the past 10 years. All died in a very short period of time.
Yes, sir. Who was the ottoman?

items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-27
items.q: Edmire Weinberg played, or Gene Mahath played clarinet.

ctx.x: Who was on the band with you?

Uh, on the band was out there with Louis, was Louis Macenta on bass. I was playing drums and vibes. Frank Pinero was playing piano. Louis played trumpet. Frank Federico played guitar. Edmire Weinberg played, or Gene Mahath played clarinet. He was a very good clarinet player. He was a very legitimate player. Good jazz player, too. So, uh, then we came, left, we left, uh, we left, uh, we left Cal, uh, left California. And we came back here and we played for about a week. Where Pete Fountains Club used to be, which…
